headline: TELEKOM'S MUNICH
AI SITE: **2X** GPUS
cover.hook_pick_reason: Names Telekom and its Munich site and states the headline fact (GPUs go from 10,000 to 20,000, slide 1) without claiming anything about Europe as a whole. Slide 2 gives the euro figure and the B300 addition; slide 4 repeats the 20 MW total. The second option shows the exact numbers but says less about who. The rivalry option covers only slide 6 (Telekom's complaint about the 60% rule, per heise), which is a side point. 'ARE DOUBLING' repeats the claim without a number. No reader-impact hook: the article states no effect on ordinary readers (what they pay, use or risk); it covers a company's capacity and its industrial customers.

slides.title: Telekom doubles its Munich AI site
body: Deutsche Telekom is doubling the capacity of its Munich AI factory from **10,000 to 20,000** Nvidia Blackwell GPUs. The site went into operation only in February, Telekom announced, as reported by heise online.

slides.title: Almost EUR 250M more
body: Telekom invests **almost EUR 250M** more in the site, per its press release, as reported by heise. The expansion adds Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs to the B200s installed earlier. After it, the site reaches **20 megawatts** of capacity.

slides.title: Booked soon after launch
body: The initial capacity is said to have been **fully booked** shortly after launch. After seven months, all installed compute was in use, heise reports.

slides.title: Built for industry
body: The site's main purpose is the **Industrial AI Cloud**. Users named by Telekom include **Siemens and Daimler Trucks**, per heise.

slides.title: A third stage is in planning
body: Telekom CEO Tim Hoettges said planning for a third stage, **Tucherpark III**, is already under way, heise reports.

slides.title: Telekom on the EU tender
body: Hoettges said Telekom is **disappointed** by the EU Gigafactory tender, mainly the rule that **60 percent** of a gigafactory's compute must be kept for the public sector. He said that would mean high idle costs, per heise.

facts.text: Deutsche Telekom is doubling the capacity of its Munich AI factory, which only went into operation in February, from 10,000 to 20,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs.
The expansion adds Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs to the B200s installed earlier.
The initial capacity is said to have been fully booked shortly after launch; after seven months all installed compute was in use.
Telekom invests almost another quarter of a billion euros (almost EUR 250M) in the site, per its press release.
After the expansion the site reaches a capacity of 20 megawatts; Telekom CEO Tim Hoettges said planning for a third stage, Tucherpark III, is already under way.
The main purpose is the Industrial AI Cloud; users named by Telekom include Siemens and Daimler Trucks.
Hoettges said Telekom is disappointed by the EU Gigafactory tender, mainly the rule that 60 percent of a gigafactory's compute must be kept for the public sector, which would mean high idle costs.

sources.title_en: Telekom upgrades AI factory in Munich, Gigafactory remains an option

caption:
Deutsche Telekom is doubling its Munich AI factory from 10,000 to 20,000 Nvidia Blackwell GPUs.

The site went into operation in February. Telekom's press release, as reported by heise online, says the investment is almost EUR 250M.

→ The expansion adds Blackwell Ultra B300 GPUs to the B200s installed earlier; the site reaches 20 megawatts
→ Initial capacity is said to have been fully booked shortly after launch; after seven months all installed compute was in use
→ Telekom CEO Tim Hoettges said planning for a third stage, Tucherpark III, is under way, and that Telekom is disappointed by the EU Gigafactory tender

What would you run on 20,000 GPUs?

Source: heise online, "Telekom upgrades AI factory in Munich, Gigafactory remains an option" (in German), Nov 9, 2026.
